title: Advanced Packaging Growth in Penang: Market Dynamics
abstract: A single number from a Penang cleanroom floor has reshaped how three analysts model the back-end supply chain.
body:
## Advanced Packaging Growth in Penang: Market Dynamics

On 2026-04-25, analysts at Maybank Investment Banking Group raised their 2026 revenue forecast for Malaysia's outsourced semiconductor assembly and test sector to 18.4 billion ringgit, up from 15.1 billion ringgit, citing advanced packaging capacity additions in Penang. The revision, circulated to institutional clients before the Kuala Lumpur open, followed a two-week channel check of substrate suppliers and cleanroom contractors on the island. It is the third upward revision in twelve months and the largest single-step change since the bank began tracking the segment in 2019.

The headline figure obscures a more consequential shift. Penang's back-end cluster, long confined to wire-bond and conventional flip-chip, is now absorbing a meaningful share of fan-out wafer-level packaging and through-silicon via work that was once the near-exclusive province of Taiwanese foundries and their captive assembly arms. TSMC's CoWoS lines remain the bottleneck for the highest-end AI accelerators, but the overflow demand for panel-level fan-out and 2.5D interposers has found a home in Batu Kawan and Bayan Lepas. That overflow is no longer marginal.

## The Substrate Squeeze

Ajey Venkatesan, a senior analyst at Maybank who covers the Malaysian technology supply chain, told clients that the binding constraint is not cleanroom space but ajinomoto build-up film substrate. "Every new fan-out line in Penang is chasing the same ABF allocation that Intel and AMD have already contracted through 2027," he wrote in the 2026-04-25 note. Venkatesan estimates that Penang's four largest OSAT operators will consume 11 percent of global ABF substrate output by the fourth quarter of 2026, up from 6 percent in the same period a year earlier.

The substrate shortage has a second-order effect on pricing. Two Penang-based assembly houses, which Venkatesan declined to name, have begun quoting fan-out wafer-level packaging at a 14 percent premium to comparable Taiwanese capacity, a reversal of the historical discount that Malaysian suppliers offered to win volume. Buyers in the United States and Europe have accepted the premium in exchange for supply-chain diversification away from the Taiwan Strait, according to three procurement managers who spoke to NotFinancialTimes on condition of anonymity.

## Equipment Orders and the Cleanroom Pipeline

Evidence of the build-out is visible in capital equipment orders. Lam Research and Applied Materials both reported a sequential increase in Southeast Asia tool shipments in their most recent quarterly disclosures, though neither company breaks out Malaysia specifically. A Penang-based distributor of wafer-handling equipment, speaking on background, said his firm's order backlog for 300-millimeter fan-out tools stretched to 41 weeks in April 2026, compared with 22 weeks in April 2025.

Cleanroom construction tells a similar story. The Penang Development Corporation has approved 1.2 million square feet of new industrial space in Batu Kawan since January 2025, of which roughly 60 percent is earmarked for semiconductor back-end uses. A construction executive involved in two of the projects said shell-and-core work is running three months behind schedule because of a shortage of ultra-pure water piping specialists, a niche trade that has not expanded fast enough to meet demand.

## The Bank of Japan Variable

Currency has become an unexpected swing factor. The Bank of Japan's decision on 2026-03-19 to widen its yield curve control band pushed the yen to 128 against the dollar, a level not seen since 2022. A weaker yen makes Japanese substrate suppliers, including Ibiden and Shinko Electric, more cost-competitive in dollar terms, which in turn pressures the pricing assumptions that Penang OSATs have built into their 2026 contracts. Venkatesan flagged the BoJ move as a risk to his 18.4 billion ringgit forecast, noting that a sustained yen below 130 could shave 400 million ringgit from the sector's export revenue.

The ringgit itself has been comparatively stable, trading in a 4.42 to 4.48 band against the dollar for most of the first quarter. Bank Negara Malaysia has kept its overnight policy rate unchanged at 3.00 percent since January 2025, providing a predictable cost of capital for the leveraged capacity expansions now underway. That stability is one reason the Penang cluster has attracted investment from Chinese OSAT operators seeking a non-China manufacturing footprint, a trend that began quietly in 2024 and accelerated through 2025.

## What the Forecast Misses

Maybank's 18.4 billion ringgit figure covers revenue booked by Malaysian-domiciled OSAT entities. It excludes the captive assembly operations that TSMC, Intel, and Samsung run inside their own Malaysian facilities, which do not sell packaging services on the open market. It also excludes the growing revenue of Singapore-based holding companies that route work through Penang subsidiaries for tax and customer-contracting reasons. Two analysts at rival brokerages, who asked not to be identified because their notes are not public, estimated that a fully consolidated figure would be 22 to 24 billion ringgit.

The more important omission may be yield. Advanced packaging in Penang remains a learning curve. A process engineer at one Batu Kawan facility said fan-out line yields were running in the low 80s as a percentage in early 2026, compared with the mid-90s that mature Taiwanese lines achieve on comparable nodes. Closing that gap is a matter of process control and operator experience, not capital. It is also the single largest determinant of whether Penang's advanced packaging growth translates into margin or merely into revenue.

For now, the direction is clear. The question for the second half of 2026 is whether substrate allocation, yen weakness, and yield learning converge to validate Maybank's number or force another revision. Venkatesan, for his part, told clients he expects to update the forecast after the June quarter earnings season. He did not indicate which way.
